answer: Each identity registers one lotus-mesh vertex to carry its signal, locking a 60-credit bond. Each vertex pays a congestion tariff each epoch, set by that epoch's count, 20 + 0.5x(count-1), published for anyone to recompute. One honest vertex pays about 20 at low load, bond back after a clean epoch. With 1000 fakes, each pays 519.50: tariffs total 519500, bonds lock 60000, growing quadratically with signal load. Each vertex binds one key; one key on two vertices burns both bonds. A load-splitting ring fails: vertices keep paying at the mesh-wide count, so batches accumulate to the full tariff.
